name: Warkay-Bipim
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Voorhoeve 1968/1975 wordlists and subgrouping notes; no grammar or phonology of Warkay-Bipim located.

sources.citation: Kriens, Ronald & Randy Lebold. 2010. Report on the Wildeman River Survey in Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2010-010.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Warkay-Bipim [bgv] only as a language related to Yaqay (p. 5); its final-stress note concerns Awyu and Yaqay, not Warkay-Bipim; no Warkay-Bipim data.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page wark1247 (refs: Voorhoeve 1968, Voorhoeve 1975, Campbell et al. 2022 ELCat, Evans et al. 2017).
sources.note: No descriptive reference listed; alt names Bipim, Bipim As-So, Warkay.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1, 345-460. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.345. Sec. 2.6.2.2.2.3.2 'Warkai-Bipim', p. 362.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent for Warkai-Bipim: p. 362 gives only a tentative phoneme inventory and says 'The wordlists do not reveal any grammatical information.' For the sister language Yaqay (p. 361): 'Drabbe describes stress in Yaqay as a kind of pitch accent; he does not indicate whether it is phonemic or not.' -- Yaqay only.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: checklist, preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. Entry no. 8 'Warkay-Bipim' and 40-item Warkay wordlist.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Checklist entry (villages Warkay, Bipim; 200-300 speakers; source Voorhoeve 1971) and a 40-item Warkay wordlist; the wordlist conventions state 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.'

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. Dutton, C. L. Voorhoeve & S. A. Wurm (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14, 47-114. Pacific Linguistics A-28. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A28.47. Sec. 3.3 'Warkai-Bipim', pp. 93-95.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 3.3.3 'The sound system' (pp. 94-95) lists 15 consonant and at least 6 vowel phonemes with allophones, word-position restrictions and consonant/vowel sequences, plus Warkai~Jakaj correspondences; no sentence on stress, accent, pitch or syllable weight. Appendix II Warkaj wordlist carries no stress marks. (A pitch/stress marking note on p. 56 belongs to the Dara section.)

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1968. The Central and South New Guinea Phylum: a report on the language situation in South New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 8, 1-17. Pacific Linguistics A-16. doi:10.15144/PL-A16.1.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistical classification of the Yaqay-Marind-Boazi family, Warkai/Bipim not mentioned.
